newsitem.title: MEXICO: DEA station chief in Mexico suddenly retires.
newsitem.headline: DEA station chief in Mexico suddenly retires.

text.p: The top United States anti-drug agent in Mexico has suddenly retired, just three months after an embarrassing failure of U.S. narcotics intelligence here.
The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) confirmed on Tuesday that its Mexico country attache, Frank David Rodriguez, had taken early retirement about three weeks ago after 27 years with the agency.

Rodriguez, 52, planned to return to the United States and take up a position with a non-governmental organisation in the Seattle area helping to attack local drug problems, said DEA spokesman Jim McGivney in Washington.

"There is nothing conspiratorial or ugly about it," McGivney said. "He's had a very long and very honourable career. Mexico is one of the toughest jobs in the DEA and he handled it well. We're sorry to see him go."

McGivney flatly denied that Rodriguez's sudden departure was in any way related to the scandal that exploded when Mexico arrested its top anti-drug officer, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, on Feb. 18 on charges of collaborating with drug lords.
Gutierrez Rebollo had attended high-level meetings with U.S. anti-drug officials and saw intelligence information about the drug war, Mexican officials said.
The affair embarrassed Washington because U.S. drug czar Barry McCaffrey had publicly praised the general only weeks earlier. U.S. officials privately blamed an intelligence failure.
Asked whether Rodriguez was being punished for the U.S. blunders over the general, McGivney said: "Absolutely not. The Mexicans failed to see it too. Everyone got caught on that one."
The U.S. embassy in Mexico City refused to comment officially on Rodriguez's departure, referring callers to the DEA in Washington.
